$schema-note: The required-test manifest of the conformance gate (scripts/conformance-gate.mjs, test/integration/check-required-tests.ts). 'required' lists the stable id of every test that MUST execute and pass in the gate: check-required-tests.ts fails the gate by id if any is missing or reported skipped, todo or failed, binds each id to its 'file', and pins required.length to EXPECTED_REQUIRED_COUNT (and 'deferred' to EXPECTED_DEFERRED_COUNT), so adding or deleting an entry without updating the pin fails the gate. Each governed test embeds its id as a [[id]] token in its title. 'deferred' lists WHERE-gated optional-feature ids, exempt while their feature is unshipped (none now).
$retirement-note: Since 2026-10-27, ids 1-4 (crash-harness.smoke.*) are kept, retargeted to a crash worker that drives the runner; ids 5-25 (the 0.9.5 crash-worker hooks, the T1/T2/T3/T5 crash tests, the soak and load-under-prune runs, P3, the differential fault schedule and its controls, the saveAndAdvance co-transaction crash) and the deferred crash.pg-kill-save.no-duplicate-with-idempotency-key are retired with the 0.9.5 parts their tests drove. 18 ids whose tests exist were added, the pinned count becoming 4 + 18 = 22; the other four (runner.crash-sweep.contents-hash-equal, runner.crash-sweep.negative-control-fires, runner.restart-20.contents-hash-equal, core.full-crash-sweep) join with the crash runs after 0.10.0, making 26. test/library-surface/retirement.test.ts checks the kept and the retired ids.

required.description: spawn the crash worker (a transaction held open before its COMMIT), SIGKILL it, confirm the shared container is still up and a fresh client connects.
pg_terminate_backend drops a targeted backend's connection and the dedicated pool recovers (reconnects with a new backend pid).
a query against a deliberately-stalled backend is bounded by a 1.5s override of the suite watchdog and throws a typed SuiteWatchdogTimeoutError, not a hang.
withSuiteWatchdog with NO explicit override applies SUITE_WATCHDOG_MS as its default bound (proven fast via fake timers, so the default is wired without a real 60s wait).
an error thrown at any point before the commit halts at h with its module and point and keeps nothing of h, on PostgreSQL and PGlite.
killed after on-start-height at a module's start h and before h commits, on-start-height fires again for h after the restart.
killed after h's COMMIT and before its on-after-db-write completed, on-after-db-write fires for h after the restart, before any callback of h + 1.
SIGTERM during on-db-write of h leaves h fully present or fully absent, and a restart resumes from the cursor.
a second writer refuses with writer-lock-held, on PostgreSQL and PGlite.
terminating the writer's backend mid-transaction gives a retryable connection-lost.
no read outside the block's transaction runs between its BEGIN and COMMIT on PGlite, under a constant read load.
negative control: reads run inside block transactions make the no-outside-read test fail.
a module's write into another module's table is rejected by the database and the block rolls back. The id is on the PostgreSQL 18 copy; the PGlite copy runs untagged (an id names one test).
the contents hash is equal on PostgreSQL and PGlite, at several page sizes.
TRUNCATE of a module's own table in a block fails with truncate-not-allowed and the block rolls back. The id is on the PostgreSQL 18 copy; the PGlite copy runs untagged (an id names one test).
killing the process with best blocks queued leaves no row of a non-finalized block, nor does the restart.
the writer's backend terminated during h's COMMIT recovers by the cursor: h kept and not processed again, h processed again, or a halt with unexpected-cursor.
reclamation by reference counting matches the reference model after every block of the DAG fixture, with the reachability check, every core_ledger_state table equal on PostgreSQL and PGlite.
a wrong ledger state root for one block halts with root-mismatch and stores nothing of that block.
core-contract-logs-full and core-contract-logs-fast give identical contract logs, on PostgreSQL 18 and PGlite.
a stopped lockstep instance makes the core wait before BEGIN, with no transaction open. The id is on the PostgreSQL 18 copy; the PGlite copy runs untagged (an id names one test).
a backup restored and resumed gives the contents hash of a process that never stopped.
